skill.name: citation-management
skill.description: Search scholarly sources, extract citation metadata, validate references, and format BibTeX for academic research workflows.
skill.summary: Manage scholarly citations with search, metadata extraction, validation, and BibTeX formatting tools.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, BibTeX examples, documentation links, placeholder API keys, DOI strings, and readable Python scripts. Confirmed risks are executable network clients, optional environment credential handling, user-directed file writes, and a Google Scholar free-proxy option. No prompt-injection override text was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Executable scripts contact external scholarly services.
remediation.suggestion: Document each network destination and require user confirmation before running scripts that contact external services.

remediation.issue: Scripts read NCBI_API_KEY and NCBI_EMAIL from the environment.
remediation.suggestion: Prompt before forwarding credentials to PubMed, and prefer explicit CLI arguments for credential use.

remediation.issue: Several scripts write or overwrite output files.
remediation.suggestion: Validate target paths, warn before overwriting existing files, and default to stdout when possible.

remediation.issue: Google Scholar search can use free proxies to avoid rate limiting.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the free-proxy option or add an explicit warning about privacy and provider policy risks.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends default schematic generation through an unbundled command.
remediation.suggestion: Move visual generation to an optional step, and include the referenced script or remove the command.

content.value_statement: Academic citation work often fails because metadata, DOIs, and BibTeX entries drift out of sync. This skill provides search, extraction, validation, and formatting workflows for reliable research references.
actual_capabilities: Search PubMed with E-utilities filters and export JSON or BibTeX results.
Search Google Scholar through the scholarly library with year and citation sorting options.
Convert DOI, PMID, arXiv, and URL identifiers into BibTeX entries.
Validate BibTeX files for missing fields, duplicate keys, invalid years, and DOI resolution.
Format, clean, sort, and deduplicate BibTeX files with standard field ordering.
Use bundled reference guides and checklists for citation quality review.
limitations: External searches require internet access and may be rate limited by providers.
Google Scholar automation depends on the third-party scholarly package.
Metadata quality depends on CrossRef, PubMed, arXiv, and publisher records.
The scripts can write output files, so review target paths before running them.

use_cases.title: Build a Literature Review Bibliography
use_cases.description: Find papers, collect metadata, and generate consistent BibTeX entries for a research review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Thesis Reference File
use_cases.description: Clean, sort, deduplicate, and validate a growing BibTeX file before submission.

use_cases.title: Check Manuscript Citations
use_cases.description: Validate DOI formats, required fields, duplicate keys, and citation completeness for publication review.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a DOI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the citation management skill to convert this DOI to a clean BibTeX entry: [DOI]. Check the author, title, journal, year, and DOI fields.

prompt_templates.title: Search PubMed
prompt_templates.prompt: Search PubMed for [topic] from [start year] to [end year]. Return the most relevant papers with citations and a short note on each result.

prompt_templates.title: Clean a BibTeX File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [file name] for duplicate entries, missing required fields, invalid years, and DOI problems. Provide a prioritized cleanup plan.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Audit a Bibliography
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a bibliography for [research question]. Search PubMed and Google Scholar, extract metadata, validate citations, and flag uncertain records for manual review.

output_examples.input: A DOI for a journal article
output_examples.output: A verified article citation with citation key, authors, title, journal, publication year, DOI, and source metadata notes.

output_examples.input: A PubMed query about immunotherapy clinical trials
output_examples.output: A ranked paper list with titles, authors, journals, years, PMIDs, abstracts when available, and suggested citation records.

output_examples.input: A BibTeX file with duplicate entries and missing fields
output_examples.output: A validation summary listing critical errors, warnings, duplicate groups, and recommended fixes before manuscript submission.

best_practices: Verify generated citations against publisher or DOI metadata before submission.
Keep output files in a project bibliography directory and review changes with version control.
Use provider API keys only when needed and keep them in environment variables.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private manuscript text into external searches unless approved.
Do not use free proxies for sensitive research queries.
Do not overwrite a shared BibTeX file without reviewing the changes.

faq.question: Can this skill search PubMed?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes PubMed E-utilities guidance and a script for searching and exporting citation metadata.

faq.question: Can it search Google Scholar?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Google Scholar workflow using the scholarly Python package.

faq.question: Does it create BibTeX entries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can convert DOI, PMID, arXiv, and URL identifiers into BibTeX-style citation entries.

faq.question: Does it validate existing references?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks required fields, years, DOI format, duplicate keys, duplicate DOIs, and optional DOI resolution.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: Most features work without API keys. NCBI keys are optional and improve PubMed rate limits.

faq.question: What should users review before running scripts?
faq.answer: Users should review network destinations, output file paths, API key handling, and provider rate limits.
